newsitem.title: USA: Virgin executive calls for more airport freedoms.
newsitem.headline: Virgin executive calls for more airport freedoms.

text.p: Airports should not restrict the profit-making opportunities of airlines' cargo activities, a top cargo executive told a group of air cargo and airport executives here Thursday.

"Airports should not restrict carriers from offering any cargo service that can add to profitability for the airlines," Angelo Pusateri, the New York-based president-cargo of Virgin Atlantic Airways told the 150 executives gathered at an air cargo symposium here.
"Some airports say we cannot handle the other carriers' cargo in our facility," Pusateri said.

Many airports restrict airlines' ability to handle cargo of other airlines. For example, at Miami International Airport, a carrier is allowed to handle the cargo of only one other airline, an airport executive said.
"Airport authorities have to have a business attitude, not a landlord attitude," Pusateri said.
The meeting is sponsored by the Airports Council International-North America, Air Freight Association, and American Association of Airport Executives.
